name: return29-foreign-plus-brokerage
description: Schedule D carries the WHOLE capital-gain story (P28): a brokerage 1099-B net total (sourced income.capital_gain.net, 20,000) coexists with the 15CA/15CB foreign-currency path (4,175,000 INR gain / 835,000 INR TDS at 83.5 = 50,000 / 10,000 USD). The FCY facts activate Schedule D, and the sourced totals FOLD INTO Part II — never dropped, never double-counted, and the legacy fed.capital_gain.net.total line is not emitted (Sch D owns the 1040 line 7).
note: HAND-VERIFIED against the PLACEHOLDER fixture rules (std deduction 15,000; ordinary brackets 10/12/22% at 10k/40k/90k; LTCG 0% to 48k then 15%). Sch D: LT = 20,000 (folded 1099-B) + 50,000 (foreign, converted) = 70,000; ST 0; line 16 = 70,000; net capital gain 70,000. Total income = 100,000 wages + 70,000 = 170,000; taxable 155,000. Ordinary portion 85,000 -> 1,000 + 3,600 + 9,900 = 14,500; all 70,000 pref stacks past the 48,000 ceiling at 15% = 10,500; tax 25,000. Form 1116: foreign-source = the 50,000 LTCG only (the brokerage gain is US-source); SS904(b)(2)(B) scale by marginal preferential / TOP ordinary rate = 15/37 (the placeholder rules carry a 37% top bracket, same as return27) -> 50,000 x 15/37 = 20,270.27 -> 20,270. Limitation = 25,000 x 20,270 / 155,000 = 3,269.03 -> 3,269. Credit = min(10,000, 3,269) = 3,269; unused 6,731. After credits 21,731; payments 15,000 -> owe 6,731.
